text: Propose by dragging into empty space: create a new graph or offer one of yours, and the owner accepts
description:
Felix 2026-11-12: when you drag from an idea into empty space in a graph you cannot write to, it asks you: create a new graph (and then leads to the login), or propose one of your existing graphs. Everyone can make a proposal, which is their graph.

From 2026-11-11, still valid here: the hypothesis of the connection is the proposer's pitch; the owner of the benefiting idea has to accept.

Today: dragging from an idea into empty space creates a supporting idea in the same graph (c3a52342); a link to a whole graph is written on the benefiting idea only, by someone who may write there (supportingRepos, with weight and hypothesis).

Missing: the offer (which graph offers to support which idea, with a pitch, by which account), showing it on the idea as not yet accepted, and accepting or declining it. Accepting writes the link with a weight into the benefiting graph.

Assumed by Claude, not said by Felix: the offer is kept on the server of the benefiting graph, outside the tracked graph, like notes (34b3d747); who may make offers follows the graph's notes setting; the new graph is created on the server the person is using, and the dragged-out idea becomes its first idea.

Not designed: an offer to a graph on another server.

status.comment: Planned 2026-11-12 at Felix's request; nothing built.
